sources.title: How to control oily skin
sources.finding: Choose oil-free, water-based makeup labeled "oil free" and "noncomedogenic"; products labeled "matte" can help reduce shine from oily skin.

sources.title: I have acne! Is it okay to wear makeup?
sources.finding: Look for one of these terms on the label: oil-free, won't clog pores, or non-comedogenic.

sources.title: Dermatologists' top tips for relieving dry skin
sources.finding: Creams add more moisture than lotions; look for ingredients such as glycerin, hyaluronic acid, dimethicone, jojoba oil and shea butter; choose products labeled "fragrance-free" (not "unscented").

sources.title: 7 rosacea skin care tips dermatologists recommend
sources.finding: Avoid products with fragrance or alcohol; test makeup first; water-based or powder makeup is less likely to irritate; a green-tinted concealer can camouflage redness; mineral (zinc oxide / titanium dioxide) sunscreens are gentler.

sources.title: Makeup Therapy for Scars (Textbook on Scar Management, ch. 49)
sources.finding: Complementary colors neutralize each other: a green corrector neutralizes redness, a yellow corrector neutralizes purplish tones such as blue-toned dark circles.

sources.title: Infraorbital Dark Circles: A Review of the Pathogenesis, Evaluation and Treatment
sources.publisher: Journal of Cutaneous and Aesthetic Surgery (PMC4924417)
sources.finding: Concealers are the least invasive option for dark circles; mineral foundation can blend uneven pigment; light-reflecting "optical diffusers" fill depressions and reflect light away from the skin.

sources.title: How To Find The Best Blush For Your Skin Tone
sources.finding: Fair: light pinks, baby roses, soft peaches. Medium: berry, rose, coral, apricot. Tan/olive: deep corals, warm roses, burnt peach, terracotta. Dark/deep: rich berries, deep plums, burnt oranges, vivid corals; sheer light shades can look ashy.

sources.title: How To Find The Perfect Blush Shade For Your Skin Tone
sources.finding: Medium to tan skin suits more orange tones; hot pink and fuchsia flatter medium-deep skin; red blush looks striking on deep skin.

sources.title: How to Use Bronzer
sources.finding: Bronzer should be one or two shades darker than your skin tone; darker is easy to overdo, lighter barely shows.

sources.title: How to Choose the Right Bronzer
sources.finding: Pick a shade slightly deeper than your natural skin tone that still works with your neck.

sources.title: Best Lipstick Colours for Tan, Deep and Dark Skin
sources.finding: Tan and deep complexions can wear deeper, bolder lip colors without being overpowered; caramel and brown-toned nudes complement deeper skin.

sources.title: The best lipsticks for your skin tone
sources.finding: Fair skin: light pink, coral, peach, nude, dusty red. The darker the skin, the deeper you need to go when selecting a color.

rules.title: Oily skin
rules.reason: Matte, shine-controlling formula for oily skin
rules.explanation: Dermatologists recommend oil-free, non-comedogenic makeup for oily skin, and say matte-labeled products help reduce shine.

rules.title: Acne / blemishes
rules.reason: Labeled oil-free or non-comedogenic, which is less likely to clog pores
rules.explanation: The AAD advises people with acne to choose makeup labeled oil-free, won't clog pores, or non-comedogenic.

rules.title: Dry skin
rules.explanation: For dry skin, dermatologists recommend richer, cream-based products with hydrating ingredients such as hyaluronic acid, glycerin, dimethicone and shea butter. Oil-absorbing (oil-control) formulas are designed for oily skin, so they're ranked lower; this part is the app's inference, not a direct dermatology recommendation.

rules.title: Sensitive skin
rules.reason: Gentle choice for sensitive skin (fragrance-free, mineral or powder)
rules.explanation: Dermatologists suggest avoiding fragrance, choosing water-based or powder makeup, skipping waterproof formulas that need harsh removers, and favoring mineral ingredients.

rules.title: Redness
rules.explanation: Green-tinted correctors neutralize red tones (complementary colors), and gentle fragrance-free, mineral formulas are less likely to trigger flushing.

rules.title: Dark circles
rules.explanation: A peer-reviewed review names concealers as the least invasive fix for dark circles, with light-reflecting particles to brighten; yellow or peach correctors neutralize bluish tones.

rules.title: Uneven skin tone
rules.reason: Buildable coverage to even out skin tone
rules.explanation: Buildable or mineral foundation can blend areas of uneven pigment, and color correctors neutralize specific tones before foundation.

rules.title: Fine lines
rules.reason: Hydrating, light-diffusing formula that softens fine lines
rules.explanation: Hydrating ingredients plump the look of skin, and light-reflecting (optical-diffusing) particles fill fine depressions and reflect light away from them.

rules.title: Texture / pores
rules.reason: Blurring finish for texture and pores
rules.explanation: Optical-diffusing particles of different sizes fill depressions in the skin and scatter light, visually smoothing texture.

fair.advice: Light pinks, baby roses and soft peaches; deep berries can look harsh.

lightMedium.advice: Roses, berries, corals and apricot show up best.

tan.advice: Deep corals, warm roses, burnt peach and terracotta; skip chalky pastels.

deep.advice: Rich berries, deep plums, burnt orange and vivid corals; sheer light shades can look ashy.

deepDark.advice: Deep fuchsia, wine, brick and warm plum pop without looking overdone.
